name: @olai/web
//exports: One subpath and STILL no root, which is the honest shape: this package has two products and neither is an import — a SCRIPT (`bun packages/web/src/build.ts <dist>`, run by default.nix and by `just build-client`) and the directory it writes — so there is no `.` for a resolver to land on. `./testlib` is the one door packages/tests is let in through (src/suite.testlib.ts, a curated list whose header says what went in and why), the same carve-out @olai/format, @olai/git, @olai/log and @olai/ops make, for the same reason. It succeeded the suite's nineteen spells of src/client/ paths, and the fence at its other end is that package's imports.test.ts.
//child: @olai/child is the subprocess socket src/build.ts rides for the Tailwind CLI. The browser bundle must never import it — this is a build-script dependency, the same carve-out `node:child_process` was.
//dependencies: @olai/surface for the wire, @olai/format for everything derived — the client computes nothing about the format on its own. @olai/fonts is the typefaces, on the entry a PAGE reads: the client draws the picker off that table. Its `./build` subpath is the other reader and the one this package's own build imports — the generated `@font-face` sheet plus the woff2 files it names, which src/build.ts appends and copies. Neither half is authored here: the package that owns the faces owns the words for them and the derivation that converts them. The remark/rehype set renders notes, documents, titles (inline-only) and the agent's replies at view time, through ONE pipeline: remark-gfm for footnotes, rehype-sanitize for what may reach innerHTML, rehype-autolink-headings for the link a heading needs before a document can be surveyed or jumped around (src/client/markdown/anchors.ts, which also says what single value the sanitiser's allowlist had to admit for them). The ID a heading is linked BY is not a dependency any more: it is @olai/format's rule (src/client/markdown/slugs.ts is the plugin that spends it), because the same slug has to be what a document's face promises and what the page lands at, and rehype-slug was a second answer to that, and rehype-highlight for fenced code — SHIPPED BY THIS SERVER rather than fetched from a CDN, which is the whole reason it is a dependency here instead of a script tag. It rides in a chunk of its own (src/client/markdown/pipeline.ts, split out by the `import()` in src/client/markdown/chunk.ts) so an outline's first paint does not carry it; same origin, same immutable /assets/ pin, still nothing asked of anyone else. `lowlight` and `highlight.js` are rehype-highlight's own dependencies, declared here because src/client/markdown/pipeline.ts imports them DIRECTLY: the `languages` option replaces the default set rather than extending it, so naming Nix means naming `lowlight`'s `common` beside it and taking the grammar off `highlight.js`. Under the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) a transitive dependency is nested where nothing outside it can see, so an undeclared one is a build that fails to resolve. @types/hast types the one tree this package walks itself (src/client/markdown/rewrite.ts, inline.ts). mdast-util-to-string is remark's own reader of the OTHER tree, and it rides in the pipeline chunk beside the parser that makes one: src/client/markdown/title.ts decides whether a title lost words by holding the text the render DREW against the text markdown reads in its source, and that second number is this utility over the mdast at its defaults (raw HTML, and an image's alt, count as text — precisely what a drawn title drops). It is already in the lockfile under mdast-util-from-markdown, which is how remark-parse reads a document at all; it is declared here because the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) hides a transitive dependency from everything outside the package that pulled it. @solid-primitives/scheduled throttles the re-render of an answer that is still arriving (src/client/chat/Entry.tsx). @olai/plugin-api is the ONLY way this client reaches a plugin, and it is a wall rather than a convenience: packages/plugin-api/src/fence.test.ts holds as an equality that no package outside the registry imports a plugin or declares one, in a module import and in a CSS import alike. So the client reaches four doors on that one package and no tenant anywhere: `@olai/plugin-api/wire` composes each plugin's sibling surface onto olai's own (src/client/wire.ts argues the whole dial), the manifest root mounts each tenant's tab half and hangs its chrome readout, `@olai/plugin-api/testids` carries the names a scenario asserts on, and `@olai/plugin-api/all.css` carries the sheets those faces need — the last of which is not optional, because Tailwind emits only what it can SEE and a face outside this tree's `@source` renders with no layout and nothing errors. @kobalte/core is the SolidJS ecosystem's accessible primitives, and it is here for the row's ••• menu (src/client/menu/NodeMenu.tsx uses its DropdownMenu, which owns being open, the placement, the two dismissals and the arrow keys), for the title-cell completions (src/client/complete/Completions.tsx hangs from the same library's popper), and for src/client/dismiss.ts, which reaches the same library one layer down (createInteractOutside / createEscapeKeyDown) so the panels this client still draws itself shut by the code the one primitive shuts by. The SolidJS rule — make full use of the ecosystem's libraries instead of hard-rolling — is the standing argument for both. The babel presets exist only for the Bun build's Solid JSX transform (src/build.ts explains why Bun's own transform cannot be used). remark-frontmatter is a DEV dependency and nothing ships it: the pipeline is deliberately innocent of the `---` block (it is one pipeline for notes and chat replies too, neither of which has frontmatter), and a document's block comes off through @olai/format's `proseIn` at the three faces that hold a whole file. The library is here for one test — src/client/markdown/frontmatter.test.ts renders each corner through it and through `proseIn` and requires the same page, so our rule cannot drift from the one GitHub and every other reader of that vault applies.
//tailwind: TWO entries, and the second is not redundant. @tailwindcss/cli is the binary src/build.ts spawns. `tailwindcss` is what `@import "tailwindcss"` inside src/client/styles.css resolves — and under the isolated linker (bunfig.toml) a transitive dependency of the CLI is nested where nothing outside it can see, so the CLI fails with "Can't resolve 'tailwindcss'" until this package declares it directly. Hoisted trees (srid/drishti) never notice; this one does.
